description: Per-game acceptance policy for the on-device scanners. Publishers embed the matching entry as `acceptancePolicy` in each game's scanner manifest (iOS format 3, Android format 2, browser index); clients keep these same values compiled in as fallbacks for manifests that predate the field, and use `default` for any game they have no entry for. Change a value here, republish the manifest, and the client behaviour changes without a code release. See docs/scanner-system/game-acceptance-policy.md.

fields.strongAcceptanceScore: Cosine similarity at which a visual top-1 is accepted with no other evidence (retry crop hypotheses add 0.02).
fields.ambiguityMargin: Minimum top-1 minus top-2 (different family) similarity; closer than this abstains unless printed evidence decides.
fields.evidenceFloor: Lowest similarity at which a candidate may be confirmed by printed evidence (title or collector number).
fields.titleGate: When an exact printed title is REQUIRED before any accept: never | binderPage | intentionalCaptures.
fields.uniqueTitleRescue: An exact, catalog-unique title confirms its visual neighbour from evidenceFloor.
fields.titleAgreementRescue: An exact title naming the same card the image ranked first (no different-name rival inside ambiguityMargin) confirms the visual family from evidenceFloor.
fields.collectorNumberScope: Which printings a footer collector number is matched against: representative | family.
fields.calibration: Free text: what the numbers were measured on.
fields.hubSimilarity: Hub rejection: similarity at which neighbours count as hub hits.
fields.hubDistinctNames: Abstain when at least this many DIFFERENT card names sit at or above hubSimilarity within the top hubTopK neighbours; genuine matches never look like that, degenerate crops (blank, glare-saturated, mis-rectified) do. 0 disables.
fields.queryNormalization: Colour normalization applied to every query crop before the encoder's resize contract: none | grey-world-autocontrast (grey-world white balance, then per-channel 1% autocontrast — Pillow semantics). Per game because it depends on what the encoder was trained on: a catalog-only encoder gains from pulling phone crops toward render statistics, an encoder trained toward camera captures loses.

pokemon.calibration: physical-v2-107fe33b; 76-label reference replay 2026-08-29: 0.65 is the smallest point above the pack/empty negatives (0.6285/0.6476). Query normalization measured OFF 2026-08-30: physical-v2 was trained toward camera captures; normalizing queries drops the 76-label replay 53 -> 49.

magic.calibration: visual-style-v2-5c27e506-r2; 49 labeled frames (sessions 2026-08-27 and 2026-08-29): plain-visual 0.65 admitted three wrong accepts at 0.64-0.69, 0.70 admitted none; simulator replay 28 -> 36 correct, 0 wrong. Hub rejection: 0 false positives on 364 verified real-camera crops, fires on 8/12 degenerate Stone Quarry attempts (2026-08-29). Query normalization 2026-08-30: on 108 labeled frames the same encoder ranks the correct family first on 79 raw vs 104 normalized crops; simulator replays 24 -> 27/29, 39 -> 47/49, 18 -> 27/30. hubDistinctNames 2: no correct crop of 160 labeled shows two different names >= 0.90; degenerate box crops do.

yugioh.calibration: Inherits the encoder-level ArcFace point; no labeled phone sessions yet.

default.calibration: Conservative profile for a game with no replay evidence: the highest measured strong-accept point, visual-first, bounded OCR rescues.
